guarantees.claim: wr_err is asserted when a register write is requested (reg_we=1) and for any address hit i, at least one byte lane has write enable (reg_be) set but the corresponding bit in KMAC_PERMIT[i] is not set, indicating an illegal partial write or access violation.

assumptions.claim: addr_hit signals are one-hot for every access; at most one bit is asserted at a time.
assumptions.risk: multiple simultaneous hits can cause incorrect wr_err, masking or falsely generating write errors, potentially leading to missed access control enforcement.

assumptions.claim: KMAC_PERMIT[i] bits are correctly configured to reflect the writable byte lanes of each register.
assumptions.risk: misconfigured permit bits may allow writes to read-only or security-sensitive register bits, causing data corruption, privilege escalation, or unexpected behavior.

assumptions.claim: reg_we, addr_hit, and reg_be are stable during the combinational evaluation and represent a valid bus transaction.
assumptions.risk: glitches or timing violations may cause false write-error assertions, leading to incorrect bus fault handling.

uncertain_points.claim: wr_err logic ORs all address hit conditions, assuming addr_hit is one-hot. If multiple addr_hit bits can be asserted simultaneously (e.g., due to address decode error), wr_err may be falsely triggered or hide a real error.
uncertain_points.cond: when multiple addr_hit bits are high
uncertain_points.risk: spurious write error could abort a valid write or mask an illegal access, leading to functional or security issues.
